name: Show Don't Tell
one_line_summary: Craft principle preferring scene and sensory detail over exposition.

name: In Medias Res
one_line_summary: Beginning a narrative in the middle of action rather than at the chronological start.

name: Neuro-Linguistic Programming
one_line_summary: Bandler and Grinder's framework linking neurology, language, and patterned behavior; widely used in coaching despite weak empirical support.
band_notes: Cultural penetration is high; specific claims about modeling excellence and neural correlates have been disconfirmed in mainstream cognitive science.

name: Spiral Dynamics
one_line_summary: Beck and Cowan's value-systems hierarchy adapted from Graves' research, used in organizational and developmental contexts.
band_notes: Adapted from Clare Graves' work but Graves himself never published comprehensive empirical validation; no peer-reviewed validation of the value-meme hierarchy.

name: Integral Theory
one_line_summary: Wilber's metasystematic synthesis integrating quadrants, levels, lines, states, and types of human development.
band_notes: Influential in transpersonal psychology and integral studies; not empirically validated and explicitly questions empirical validation as sole criterion of truth.

name: Pomodoro Technique
one_line_summary: Cirillo's time-management technique using 25-minute focus intervals separated by short breaks.

name: Basel III
one_line_summary: Bank capital, leverage, and liquidity standards from the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision, post-2008.
band_notes: Implemented through national regulators with local variation; Basel IV finalization is in progress.

name: CAMELS Rating
one_line_summary: US bank examination rating: Capital, Assets, Management, Earnings, Liquidity, Sensitivity to market risk.

name: Dodd-Frank Act
one_line_summary: US 2010 financial reform legislation establishing CFPB, FSOC, Volcker Rule, and resolution authority.

name: BSA/AML
one_line_summary: US framework requiring financial institutions to detect and report suspicious activity.

name: KYC
one_line_summary: Customer due diligence requirements identifying who is doing business with a financial institution.

name: Community Reinvestment Act
one_line_summary: US 1977 law requiring banks to meet credit needs of all communities they serve, including low-income areas.

name: FFIEC IT Examination Handbook
one_line_summary: Federal Financial Institutions Examination Council guidance for examining IT operations at supervised institutions.

name: CCAR
one_line_summary: Federal Reserve's annual capital adequacy assessment of large bank holding companies.

name: DFAST
one_line_summary: Annual stress testing required for banks above asset thresholds under Dodd-Frank.

name: CECL
one_line_summary: US GAAP standard requiring forward-looking estimation of expected credit losses over instrument lifetime.

name: IFRS 9
one_line_summary: International accounting standard for financial instruments, including expected credit loss model.

name: ALCO Framework
one_line_summary: Bank governance framework for managing interest rate risk, liquidity, and balance sheet structure.
band_notes: Conceptual governance framework rather than a codified standard; specific structure varies considerably across institutions.

name: Sarbanes-Oxley
one_line_summary: US 2002 law mandating financial reporting controls and executive certifications for public companies.

name: COSO Internal Control-Integrated Framework
one_line_summary: Five-component framework for designing internal controls: control environment, risk assessment, control activities, information and communication, monitoring.

name: COSO ERM
one_line_summary: Enterprise-level extension of COSO internal control framework integrating strategy and performance with risk.

name: ISO 31000
one_line_summary: International standard providing principles and generic guidelines on risk management.

name: Three Lines Model
one_line_summary: IIA framework distinguishing operational management, risk and compliance functions, and internal audit assurance.
band_notes: 2020 IIA update renamed and refined the older 'Three Lines of Defense' framing; conceptual framework rather than a codified standard.

name: FAIR
one_line_summary: Quantitative risk framework decomposing risk into loss event frequency and loss magnitude with probabilistic factors.
band_notes: Quantitative methodology now standardized as Open FAIR through The Open Group; distinct from qualitative risk-rating approaches.

name: ORSA
one_line_summary: Insurance-sector self-assessment of all material risks against capital and solvency.

name: NIST Cybersecurity Framework
one_line_summary: Six core functions (Govern, Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond, Recover) plus implementation tiers and profiles.

name: NIST 800-53
one_line_summary: Catalog of security and privacy controls for federal information systems and organizations.

name: NIST Risk Management Framework
one_line_summary: Seven-step process for integrating security, privacy, and risk management into the system development lifecycle.

name: ISO/IEC 27001
one_line_summary: International standard specifying requirements for an information security management system (ISMS).

name: ISO/IEC 27002
one_line_summary: International standard providing guidance on information security controls.

name: CIS Controls
one_line_summary: Center for Internet Security's prioritized set of cybersecurity actions for organizations.

name: MITRE ATT&CK
one_line_summary: Globally accessible knowledge base of adversary tactics, techniques, and procedures based on real-world observations.
band_notes: Knowledge base structure rather than a prescriptive control framework; widely used as reference and threat-modeling input.

name: Cyber Kill Chain
one_line_summary: Seven-phase model of intrusion: reconnaissance, weaponization, delivery, exploitation, installation, command-and-control, actions on objectives.
band_notes: Lockheed Martin's framework biases toward perimeter-centric thinking; less aligned with cloud and zero-trust architectures.

name: Diamond Model of Intrusion Analysis
one_line_summary: Four-feature framework for intrusion events: adversary, capability, infrastructure, victim.

name: STRIDE
one_line_summary: Microsoft threat modeling categorization: Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Information disclosure, Denial of service, Elevation of privilege.

name: PASTA
aliases: Process for Attack Simulation and Threat Analysis
one_line_summary: Seven-stage risk-centric threat modeling methodology.

name: Zero Trust Architecture
one_line_summary: Security model assuming no implicit trust based on network location; every access decision is verified.
band_notes: Coined by Forrester's John Kindervag; codified into NIST 800-207 for operational guidance.

name: Defense in Depth
one_line_summary: Strategy using multiple overlapping security controls so failure of any single layer does not compromise the system.

name: CMMC
one_line_summary: DoD certification framework for protecting federal contract information and controlled unclassified information.

name: HITRUST CSF
one_line_summary: Certifiable framework integrating HIPAA, NIST, ISO, PCI, and other authoritative sources.

name: FedRAMP
aliases: Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program
one_line_summary: US government program standardizing security assessment and authorization for cloud services.

name: PCI DSS
aliases: Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard
one_line_summary: Industry standard for organizations handling branded credit cards from major card networks.

name: GDPR
one_line_summary: EU regulation on data protection and privacy applicable to processing of EU residents' personal data.
band_notes: Has substantial extraterritorial reach; non-EU organizations processing EU residents' data must comply.

name: CCPA
one_line_summary: California state law granting consumers rights over personal information collected by businesses.

name: HIPAA
aliases: Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act
one_line_summary: US law establishing privacy and security standards for protected health information.

name: Privacy by Design
one_line_summary: Cavoukian's seven foundational principles for embedding privacy into the design of systems and processes.

name: FIPPs
one_line_summary: Foundational set of principles (notice, choice, access, security, accountability) underlying most privacy regimes.

name: Differential Privacy
one_line_summary: Formal definition guaranteeing that the inclusion or exclusion of any single record does not significantly affect query outputs.

name: ISO 9001
one_line_summary: International standard for quality management systems with seven principles including process approach and continuous improvement.

name: ITIL
one_line_summary: Framework for IT service management including service strategy, design, transition, operation, and continual improvement.

name: COBIT
aliases: Control Objectives for Information and Related Technologies
one_line_summary: ISACA framework for governance and management of enterprise IT.

name: TOGAF
one_line_summary: Enterprise architecture framework with Architecture Development Method (ADM) and content metamodel.

name: Zachman Framework
one_line_summary: Enterprise architecture taxonomy intersecting six perspectives with six abstractions (what, how, where, who, when, why).

name: CMMI
one_line_summary: Five-level process maturity model: Initial, Managed, Defined, Quantitatively Managed, Optimizing.

name: SOC 2
one_line_summary: AICPA framework for reporting on controls relevant to security, availability, processing integrity, confidentiality, and privacy.

name: SSAE 18
one_line_summary: Statement on Standards for Attestation Engagements 18 — current AICPA standard governing service organization audits.

name: TCFD
aliases: Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures
one_line_summary: Voluntary framework for climate-related financial risk disclosures across governance, strategy, risk, and metrics.

name: SASB
one_line_summary: Industry-specific sustainability disclosure standards, now under the IFRS Foundation's ISSB.

name: GRI
one_line_summary: Most widely used sustainability reporting framework with universal, sector, and topic standards.

name: LEED
aliases: Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design
one_line_summary: USGBC certification system for green buildings across categories like energy, water, materials, and indoor environment.

name: PMBOK Guide
one_line_summary: PMI's Project Management Body of Knowledge defining processes, knowledge areas, and the basis for the PMP certification.

name: PRINCE2
one_line_summary: AXELOS's process-based project management methodology widely used in UK government and international contexts.

name: PRINCE2 Agile
one_line_summary: AXELOS framework composing PRINCE2 governance with agile delivery techniques drawn primarily from DSDM and Scrum.

name: IPMA Competence Baseline
one_line_summary: International Project Management Association's competence-based framework for individual project, programme, and portfolio managers.

name: ISO 21500
one_line_summary: International standard providing guidance on project management concepts and processes, foundational to the ISO 21500 series.

name: ISO 21502
one_line_summary: International standard providing guidance on project management practices, replacing ISO 21500:2012 as the practice-focused standard.

name: P3.express
one_line_summary: Open-license lightweight project management methodology designed for medium-sized organizations.

name: OPM3
one_line_summary: PMI's framework assessing an organization's project management maturity across knowledge, assessment, and improvement domains.

name: P3M3
aliases: Portfolio Programme Project Management Maturity Model
one_line_summary: AXELOS maturity model assessing organizational capability across portfolio, programme, and project management.

name: Managing Successful Programmes
one_line_summary: AXELOS programme management methodology for delivering transformational change through coordinated projects.

name: Management of Risk
one_line_summary: AXELOS risk management methodology providing principles, approach, processes, and techniques across organizational levels.

name: DSDM
one_line_summary: Agile project delivery framework emphasizing fixed time and cost with variable scope, foundational to PRINCE2 Agile.

name: Crystal Methods
one_line_summary: Cockburn's family of agile methodologies sized to project criticality and team size, ranging from Crystal Clear to Crystal Magenta.

name: Feature-Driven Development
one_line_summary: Iterative development methodology organized around designing and building client-valued features in short iterations.

name: Rational Unified Process
one_line_summary: IBM's iterative software development process organized around inception, elaboration, construction, and transition phases.

name: Disciplined Agile
one_line_summary: PMI's hybrid agile framework providing a toolkit of practices drawn from Scrum, Kanban, XP, and other sources.

name: Nexus
one_line_summary: Scrum.org's framework for scaling Scrum across multiple teams working on a single product.

name: Scrum at Scale
one_line_summary: Sutherland's framework for scaling Scrum across an organization through Scrum of Scrums and Executive Action Teams.

name: Critical Path Method
one_line_summary: Network analysis technique identifying the longest sequence of dependent activities and the project duration they determine.

name: PERT
one_line_summary: Probabilistic project scheduling technique using three-point estimates to model activity duration uncertainty.

name: Critical Chain Project Management
one_line_summary: Goldratt's application of Theory of Constraints to project management, replacing task-level safety with project-level buffers.

name: Earned Value Management
one_line_summary: Project performance measurement integrating scope, schedule, and cost; standardized in ANSI/EIA-748 and required in US federal contracting.

name: Gantt Chart Methodology
one_line_summary: Time-decomposition framework visualizing tasks as horizontal bars on a timeline, originating with Henry Gantt's industrial scheduling work.

name: Last Planner System
one_line_summary: Lean construction scheduling framework emphasizing pull planning, weekly work plans, and learning from variance.

name: DoD 5000 Series
one_line_summary: US Department of Defense's framework governing acquisition of weapons systems and other major defense programs.

name: NASA NPR 7120.5
one_line_summary: NASA Procedural Requirements governing program and project management for spaceflight and research.

name: ICH-GCP
one_line_summary: International Council for Harmonisation guidelines for the design, conduct, and reporting of clinical trials involving human subjects.

name: Construction Manager at Risk
one_line_summary: Construction project delivery method in which the construction manager commits to deliver within a guaranteed maximum price.

name: Integrated Project Delivery
one_line_summary: Collaborative construction project delivery method aligning contracts, risk-sharing, and team integration around shared outcomes.

name: Design-Bid-Build
one_line_summary: Traditional construction project delivery method with sequential design, competitive bidding, and construction phases under separate contracts.

name: Design-Build
one_line_summary: Construction project delivery method consolidating design and construction responsibilities under a single contract.

name: Annales School
one_line_summary: French historical school emphasizing long-duration structural history (longue durée), mentalités, and social-scientific integration over event-history.

name: Marxist Historiography
one_line_summary: Historical analysis treating class struggle, modes of production, and material conditions as the primary engines of historical change.

name: Whig History
one_line_summary: Progressivist historical narrative reading the past as inevitable advance toward present liberal institutions, named and critiqued by Herbert Butterfield.

name: Great Man Theory
one_line_summary: Carlyle's view of history as fundamentally the biography of exceptional individuals; widely critiqued and largely abandoned in academic history.

name: Cambridge School
one_line_summary: Skinner and Pocock's contextualist approach to intellectual history, recovering historical meaning through linguistic and contextual reconstruction.

name: Microhistory
one_line_summary: Italian historical school using detailed reconstruction of small-scale events and individuals to illuminate broader historical patterns.

name: Counterfactual History
one_line_summary: Historical method using disciplined speculation about alternative outcomes to illuminate causation and contingency in actual events.

name: History from Below
one_line_summary: Historical approach reconstructing the experiences and agency of ordinary people, workers, and marginalized groups rather than elites.

name: Postcolonial History
one_line_summary: Historical approach critiquing colonial frameworks and recovering perspectives marginalized by colonial-era historiography.

name: Linguistic Turn
one_line_summary: Hayden White's and others' framework treating historical writing as fundamentally narrative construction shaped by rhetorical and linguistic choices.

name: Big History
one_line_summary: David Christian's framework presenting history as a unified narrative from cosmic origins through the present, integrating multiple disciplines.

name: Environmental History
one_line_summary: Historical approach foregrounding human-environment interaction as a central driver of historical change, associated with Crosby and Worster.

name: Subaltern Studies
one_line_summary: South Asian historical school recovering the agency and consciousness of subaltern groups, originating with Ranajit Guha's collective.

name: Source Criticism
one_line_summary: Niebuhr and Ranke's methodology for classifying and evaluating historical sources for authenticity, authority, and bias.

name: Prosopography
one_line_summary: Historical method analyzing groups through systematic biographical data on their members to reveal social and political patterns.

name: Oral History Methodology
one_line_summary: Systematic recording, transcription, and analysis of personal testimony as historical evidence, especially for underdocumented populations.

name: Cliometrics
one_line_summary: Application of quantitative methods and economic theory to historical analysis, foundational to modern economic history.

name: Comparative Historical Analysis
one_line_summary: Skocpol and Tilly's methodology systematically comparing historical cases to identify causal patterns in macro-social processes.

name: Hegelian Dialectic
one_line_summary: Hegel's framework of historical and conceptual development through thesis-antithesis-synthesis, foundational to subsequent dialectical traditions.

name: Vico's Corsi e Ricorsi
one_line_summary: Giambattista Vico's cyclical theory of historical recurrence through ages of gods, heroes, and men, articulated in the New Science.

name: Spenglerian Cycles
one_line_summary: Oswald Spengler's morphological theory treating civilizations as organic entities with predictable life cycles of growth and decline.

name: Toynbee's Civilizations
one_line_summary: Arnold Toynbee's framework analyzing twenty-one civilizations through their responses to environmental and historical challenges.

name: Kondratiev Waves
one_line_summary: Approximately fifty-year economic cycles theorized by Nikolai Kondratiev, later integrated with Schumpeterian innovation theory.
band_notes: Empirical evidence for the cycle's regularity is contested; the framework has been more influential in heterodox economics than in mainstream macroeconomics.

name: Demographic Transition Theory
one_line_summary: Stage model describing how populations move from high birth and death rates to low rates as societies industrialize, associated with Notestein.

name: Malthusian Trap
one_line_summary: Thomas Malthus's theory that population growth eventually outpaces food production, producing recurring crises of subsistence.
band_notes: Strong-form predictions have been substantially falsified in modern economies; weak-form applications to pre-industrial societies remain influential through the Clark hypothesis and unified growth theory.

name: Hayden White's Tropics
one_line_summary: Hayden White's framework analyzing historical writing through four master tropes (metaphor, metonymy, synecdoche, irony) governing emplotment.

name: Theosophy
one_line_summary: Blavatsky's synthetic spiritual system describing hidden masters, root races, and planes of existence; foundational to modern Western esotericism.
band_notes: Specific historical and metaphysical claims (root races, hidden masters in Tibet) have no empirical support and the framework's race-evolutionary apparatus has been criticized as proto-racialist; influence on later esoteric movements is nonetheless substantial.

name: Anthroposophy
one_line_summary: Rudolf Steiner's spiritual science framework describing spiritual hierarchies, etheric and astral bodies, and karmic evolution; basis of Waldorf education and biodynamic agriculture.
band_notes: Specific spiritual-scientific claims have no empirical support; Waldorf education and biodynamic agriculture have practitioner adoption but limited rigorous evidence base for their distinctive claims.

name: Hermeticism
one_line_summary: Western esoteric tradition descending from late-antique Greek-Egyptian texts attributed to Hermes Trismegistus, organized around principles like 'as above, so below' and the seven Hermetic principles.

name: Hermetic Qabalah
one_line_summary: Western occult adaptation of Jewish Kabbalistic Tree of Life integrated with Hermetic, Tarot, and astrological correspondences; distinct from traditional Jewish Kabbalah.
band_notes: Often conflated with traditional Jewish Kabbalah but represents a substantially different tradition with different sources, practitioners, and aims.

name: Thelema
one_line_summary: Aleister Crowley's spiritual system organized around the Law of Thelema ('Do what thou wilt') and the doctrine of True Will.

name: Rosicrucianism
one_line_summary: Western esoteric tradition originating in early-17th-century manifestos and continued through modern organizations like AMORC and the Rosicrucian Fellowship.
band_notes: Contemporary Rosicrucian organizations differ substantially in lineage, practice, and authority; the original manifesto authors remain unidentified.

name: Neo-Platonic Emanation
one_line_summary: Plotinus's cosmological framework of reality emanating from the One through the Nous (Intellect) and Soul down to matter; profoundly influential on Christian, Islamic, and Jewish mystical traditions.

name: Gnosticism
one_line_summary: Late-antique religious tradition organized around the demiurge-pleroma-sophia cosmology and salvation through gnosis (direct knowledge of divine reality).

name: Fourth Way
one_line_summary: Gurdjieff and Ouspensky's framework integrating self-remembering, the three centers, and the enneagram of process (distinct from the personality enneagram) toward conscious development.
band_notes: Gurdjieff's source claims (Sarmoung Brotherhood) are unverifiable; the system's effectiveness claims rest on practitioner testimony rather than empirical evaluation.

name: A Course in Miracles
one_line_summary: Helen Schucman's spiritual text and curriculum synthesizing Christian language with Vedantic non-dualism, organized around the distinction between the ego and the Holy Spirit.

name: Swedenborgianism
one_line_summary: Emanuel Swedenborg's framework of correspondences between spiritual and natural worlds; influential on Blake, Emerson, James, and Borges.

name: The White Goddess
one_line_summary: Robert Graves's mythopoetic framework arguing for a single triple-goddess archetype underlying European mythology and poetic inspiration.
band_notes: Specific historical claims about pre-Christian European goddess religion have been rejected by mainstream classical scholarship; influence on second-wave feminism, neopaganism, and Joseph Campbell is nonetheless substantial.

name: Orgone Theory
one_line_summary: Wilhelm Reich's theory of a universal life-force energy claimed to be physically measurable and accumulable through specially constructed devices.
band_notes: Specific empirical claims about orgone energy have been comprehensively rejected by physics; orgone accumulators were prohibited by FDA injunction in 1954. The framework persists primarily in alternative-medicine and esoteric contexts rather than physics or contemplative practice.

name: Family Constellations
one_line_summary: Bert Hellinger's therapeutic methodology using group representation of family members to surface and resolve transgenerational dynamics.
band_notes: No rigorous empirical support for the methodology's distinctive claims about systemic transmission; some clinical adoption in continental European contexts but not widely accepted in mainstream psychotherapy.

name: Principled Negotiation
one_line_summary: Fisher and Ury's framework separating people from problem, focusing on interests rather than positions, generating options, and using objective criteria.

name: BATNA
aliases: Best Alternative to a Negotiated Agreement
one_line_summary: Fisher and Ury's concept of one's best fallback option outside the current negotiation, used as the threshold for accepting any agreement.

name: ZOPA
one_line_summary: The range between parties' reservation prices within which any agreement is mutually acceptable.

name: Integrative vs Distributive Bargaining
one_line_summary: Walton and McKersie's foundational distinction between negotiations expanding joint value and negotiations dividing fixed value.

name: Thomas-Kilmann Conflict Mode Instrument
one_line_summary: Five-mode framework for conflict-handling styles: competing, collaborating, compromising, avoiding, accommodating.
band_notes: Empirical support is moderate; the instrument's psychometric properties are weaker than its widespread organizational use suggests.

name: Nonviolent Communication
one_line_summary: Marshall Rosenberg's framework structuring communication around observation, feeling, need, and request.
band_notes: Practitioner adoption is substantial but rigorous empirical validation is limited; some critics have noted that the method's self-presentation as 'nonviolent' begs the question.

name: Interest-Based Relational Approach
one_line_summary: Conflict-resolution approach prioritizing relationship preservation alongside interest satisfaction.

name: Difficult Conversations Framework
one_line_summary: Stone, Patton, and Heen's framework distinguishing the 'what happened' conversation, the feelings conversation, and the identity conversation.

name: Crucial Conversations
one_line_summary: Patterson, Grenny, McMillan, and Switzler's framework for high-stakes conversations involving strong emotions and opposing opinions.

name: Transformative Mediation
one_line_summary: Bush and Folger's mediation framework focused on empowering parties and fostering recognition rather than reaching settlement.

name: Facilitative Mediation
one_line_summary: Mediation framework in which the mediator facilitates communication and negotiation without offering opinions on the merits.

name: Evaluative Mediation
one_line_summary: Mediation framework in which the mediator offers opinions on the strengths and weaknesses of parties' positions and likely outcomes.

name: Restorative Circles
one_line_summary: Restorative practice framework using structured group dialogue to address harm, develop understanding, and rebuild relationships.

name: Dialogic Organization Development
one_line_summary: Bushe and Marshak's framework treating organizational change as emerging from shifts in conversation and meaning-making rather than diagnostic interventions.

name: Powell Doctrine
one_line_summary: Colin Powell's set of decision criteria for committing US military force, including clear objectives, public support, and exit strategy.

name: Deliberate Practice
one_line_summary: Anders Ericsson's framework characterizing the specific, effortful, feedback-driven practice associated with expert performance.
band_notes: The popular ten-thousand-hours formulation oversimplifies Ericsson's research; subsequent work (Macnamara et al.) has shown that deliberate practice explains less variance in expert performance than originally claimed.

name: Periodization
one_line_summary: Matveyev's framework structuring athletic training in cycles of varying intensity and volume to optimize peak performance.

name: Long-Term Athlete Development
one_line_summary: Istvan Balyi's framework describing athletic development phases across the lifespan, used in national sport development systems.

name: Coerver Method
one_line_summary: Wiel Coerver's skill-based soccer coaching methodology emphasizing individual ball mastery through structured progression.

name: Mental Skills Training
one_line_summary: Sport psychology toolkit covering goal-setting, imagery, self-talk, arousal regulation, and concentration applied to athletic performance.

name: Inner Game
one_line_summary: Timothy Gallwey's framework distinguishing the conscious 'Self 1' from the embodied 'Self 2' in performance contexts; widely influential beyond sports.

name: Marginal Gains
one_line_summary: Dave Brailsford's framework systematically pursuing one-percent improvements across many small factors, associated with British Cycling's competitive success.

name: Superforecasting
one_line_summary: Philip Tetlock's framework characterizing the practices and dispositions associated with consistently accurate forecasting under uncertainty.

name: Scenario Planning (Wack)
one_line_summary: Pierre Wack's narrative scenario methodology developed at Royal Dutch Shell, focused on shifting executives' mental models rather than predicting futures.

name: Reference Class Forecasting
one_line_summary: Kahneman and Tversky's method, developed for projects by Bent Flyvbjerg, using base rates from comparable past cases to correct for the planning fallacy.

name: Prediction Markets
one_line_summary: Aggregating dispersed information about future events through trading mechanisms that produce price-based probability estimates.

name: Foresight Cone
one_line_summary: Voros's framework distinguishing possible, plausible, probable, and preferable futures across an expanding cone of uncertainty.

name: Causal Layered Analysis
one_line_summary: Sohail Inayatullah's four-layer futures methodology analyzing the litany, social causes, worldviews, and myths underlying any contested future.

name: Backcasting
one_line_summary: Foresight method working backward from a desired future state to identify the actions and decisions needed to reach it.

name: Delphi Method
one_line_summary: RAND-developed structured method for eliciting expert consensus through iterated anonymous rounds with controlled feedback.

name: Self-Organized Criticality
one_line_summary: Per Bak's framework characterizing systems that naturally tune themselves to critical states producing power-law-distributed avalanches, originating with the sandpile model.

name: Statistical Complexity
one_line_summary: Crutchfield's measure of the size of the minimal predictive model of a stochastic process, explicitly designed to distinguish complex from random processes.

name: Effective Complexity
one_line_summary: Gell-Mann and Lloyd's measure separating regular from random components in a description, capturing the structured rather than random part.

name: Logical Depth
one_line_summary: Charles Bennett's measure of the computational resources required to produce an object from its shortest description, capturing how much 'work' a structured object encodes.

name: Fractal Dimension
one_line_summary: Generalization of integer dimension capturing the scaling behavior of self-similar objects, formalized through Mandelbrot's work and earlier Hausdorff measure theory.

name: Extended Evolutionary Synthesis
one_line_summary: Research programme extending the Modern Synthesis to incorporate developmental plasticity, niche construction, inclusive inheritance, and evolvability.
band_notes: Disputed within mainstream evolutionary biology about whether the proposed extensions add explanatory power beyond the standard Modern Synthesis.

name: NIST AI Risk Management Framework
one_line_summary: NIST's voluntary framework for managing AI risks across govern, map, measure, and manage functions, released January 2023 with a generative AI profile in 2024.

name: EU AI Act
one_line_summary: European Union regulation establishing a risk-based framework for AI systems, including prohibited practices, high-risk requirements, and general-purpose AI obligations.

name: ISO/IEC 42001
one_line_summary: International standard specifying requirements for an AI management system (AIMS), published 2023.

name: OECD AI Principles
one_line_summary: Intergovernmental principles for trustworthy AI adopted by OECD members and partner countries, foundational to subsequent AI governance frameworks.

name: Singapore Model AI Governance Framework
one_line_summary: Singapore IMDA's voluntary framework for organizational AI governance, including a generative AI extension.

name: AI Bill of Rights
aliases: Blueprint for an AI Bill of Rights
one_line_summary: US Office of Science and Technology Policy's blueprint articulating five principles for automated systems affecting Americans' rights.
band_notes: Non-binding blueprint rather than enforceable regulation; superseded in regulatory effect by subsequent executive orders.

name: NIST Privacy Framework
one_line_summary: NIST's voluntary privacy risk management framework parallel in structure to the Cybersecurity Framework, with identify-govern-control-communicate-protect functions.

name: FFIEC AIO Booklet
one_line_summary: Federal Financial Institutions Examination Council's IT Examination Handbook booklet covering architecture, infrastructure, and operational practices.

name: OCC Heightened Standards
one_line_summary: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency's heightened risk governance standards applicable to large national banks above asset thresholds.

name: Model Risk Management
one_line_summary: Federal Reserve and OCC supervisory guidance establishing the foundational US framework for identifying, assessing, and controlling model risk in financial institutions.

name: NIST 800-171
one_line_summary: NIST publication specifying security requirements for protecting controlled unclassified information in nonfederal systems; foundational to CMMC.

name: OCC Risk Governance Framework
one_line_summary: Risk governance component of the OCC Heightened Standards specifying board, management, and three-lines requirements for large banks.

name: Job Characteristics Model
one_line_summary: Hackman and Oldham's framework relating five job characteristics (skill variety, task identity, task significance, autonomy, feedback) to motivation and performance through critical psychological states.

name: Equity Theory
one_line_summary: J. Stacy Adams's framework explaining workplace motivation through perceived fairness of input-outcome ratios compared to relevant others.

name: Expectancy Theory
one_line_summary: Victor Vroom's framework characterizing motivation as the product of expectancy (effort-performance), instrumentality (performance-outcome), and valence (outcome value).

name: Goal-Setting Theory
one_line_summary: Locke and Latham's framework establishing that specific, challenging goals improve performance more than vague or easy goals, mediated by attention, effort, persistence, and strategy.

name: Resource Dependence Theory
one_line_summary: Pfeffer and Salancik's framework treating organizations as fundamentally shaped by their dependence on external resources and the strategies they use to manage that dependence.

name: Institutional Theory
one_line_summary: DiMaggio and Powell's framework explaining organizational similarity through coercive, mimetic, and normative isomorphic pressures and the pursuit of legitimacy.

name: Population Ecology of Organizations
one_line_summary: Hannan and Freeman's framework treating organizational populations as subject to selection pressures analogous to biological evolution.

name: Garbage Can Model
one_line_summary: Cohen, March, and Olsen's framework characterizing decision-making in organized anarchies as the chance confluence of problems, solutions, participants, and choice opportunities.

name: Bounded Rationality
one_line_summary: Herbert Simon's framework treating human decision-making as constrained by cognitive limits, information costs, and time pressure rather than approximating ideal rationality.

name: Recognition-Primed Decision Making
one_line_summary: Gary Klein's framework characterizing how experts make rapid decisions by recognizing situations as similar to past cases and mentally simulating the recognized response.

name: Naturalistic Decision Making
one_line_summary: Klein, Zsambok, and others' research programme studying how people actually make decisions in real-world high-stakes settings rather than laboratory conditions.

name: Implementation Intentions
one_line_summary: Peter Gollwitzer's framework using specific if-then plans linking situational cues to intended responses to bridge the intention-behavior gap.

name: Tiny Habits
one_line_summary: BJ Fogg's behavior-change framework anchoring new minimum-viable behaviors to existing routines and celebrating immediate success.

name: Atomic Habits
one_line_summary: James Clear's framework characterizing habit formation through the cue-craving-response-reward loop and four laws of behavior change.
band_notes: Practitioner-oriented synthesis of existing behavioral psychology rather than original empirical research.

name: Lindy Effect
one_line_summary: Nassim Taleb's formulation of an empirical regularity (originally attributed to Mandelbrot and earlier observers) that the future life expectancy of non-perishable things scales with their current age.

name: Antifragility
one_line_summary: Nassim Taleb's framework characterizing systems that gain rather than lose from disorder, volatility, and stress, distinct from both fragility and resilience.

name: Black Swan Theory
one_line_summary: Nassim Taleb's framework characterizing high-impact rare events that are unpredictable in advance, rationalized after the fact, and undersampled by historical experience.

name: Double-Entry Bookkeeping
one_line_summary: Foundational logic of accounting representing every economic event as offsetting debits and credits across two or more accounts, codified by Pacioli in 1494 and underlying all modern accounting systems.

name: US GAAP
aliases: Generally Accepted Accounting Principles; FASB ASC
one_line_summary: Body of accounting standards governing US financial reporting, codified in the FASB Accounting Standards Codification.

name: IFRS
one_line_summary: IASB's body of accounting standards used across most of the developed world outside the United States.

name: GASB
one_line_summary: Body of accounting standards governing US state and local governmental entities, established in 1984.

name: FASAB
one_line_summary: Body of accounting standards governing US federal government financial reporting.

name: IPSAS
one_line_summary: International accounting standards for public sector entities, the public sector counterpart to IFRS.

name: ASC 606
one_line_summary: FASB Accounting Standards Codification topic establishing a five-step framework for revenue recognition; converged with IFRS 15.

name: ASC 842
one_line_summary: FASB topic requiring most leases to be recognized on the balance sheet as right-of-use assets and lease liabilities.

name: ASC 815
one_line_summary: FASB topic governing recognition, measurement, and disclosure of derivative instruments and hedging activities.

name: ASC 805
one_line_summary: FASB topic governing the acquisition method of accounting for business combinations including goodwill and intangible asset recognition.

name: IFRS 15
one_line_summary: IASB standard for revenue recognition; converged with ASC 606 through the FASB-IASB joint revenue project.

name: IFRS 16
one_line_summary: IASB standard requiring lessees to recognize most leases on the balance sheet, parallel in intent to ASC 842 with implementation differences.

name: IFRS 17
one_line_summary: IASB standard establishing recognition, measurement, and disclosure principles for insurance contracts, effective 2023.

name: FASB Conceptual Framework
one_line_summary: FASB's foundational framework articulating qualitative characteristics, elements, recognition, and measurement principles underlying US GAAP standard-setting.

name: IASB Conceptual Framework
one_line_summary: IASB's foundational framework articulating the objectives, qualitative characteristics, and recognition principles underlying IFRS standard-setting.

name: GAAS
one_line_summary: AICPA's body of auditing standards governing US private company audits, organized into general, fieldwork, and reporting standards.

name: PCAOB Auditing Standards
one_line_summary: Public Company Accounting Oversight Board's auditing standards governing audits of US public companies, established by Sarbanes-Oxley.

name: ISA
one_line_summary: IAASB's international auditing standards used in over 130 jurisdictions globally.

name: Yellow Book
one_line_summary: GAO's Generally Accepted Government Auditing Standards governing audits of US government entities and federal funds.

name: Accrual Accounting
one_line_summary: Recognition principle recording revenues when earned and expenses when incurred regardless of cash timing; the foundation of modern financial reporting.

name: Cash Accounting
one_line_summary: Recognition principle recording transactions when cash changes hands; permitted for smaller entities and tax purposes in some jurisdictions.

name: Activity-Based Costing
one_line_summary: Cooper and Kaplan's cost allocation framework assigning overhead to products based on activities consumed rather than volume-based allocation.

name: Throughput Accounting
one_line_summary: Goldratt's TOC-derived alternative to standard cost accounting prioritizing throughput, inventory, and operating expense over conventional cost allocation.

name: Lean Accounting
one_line_summary: Accounting methodology aligned with lean operations, replacing standard cost variance analysis with value-stream costing and visual management.

name: Triple-Entry Accounting
one_line_summary: Ian Grigg's cryptographic extension of double-entry bookkeeping using digitally signed receipts as a third record verifiable across parties; foundational to blockchain accounting concepts.

name: Fund Accounting
one_line_summary: Accounting framework for nonprofit and governmental entities organizing financial activity around restricted-purpose funds rather than profit-loss tracking.

name: Tax Basis Accounting
one_line_summary: Accounting framework for measuring transactions according to applicable tax law rather than GAAP or IFRS, used for tax filing purposes.

name: Statutory Accounting Principles
one_line_summary: Accounting framework for US insurance companies established by NAIC, emphasizing solvency over earnings measurement.

name: Cost Accounting Standards
one_line_summary: Accounting standards established by the Cost Accounting Standards Board governing US government contractor cost allocation and measurement.

name: Circle of Fifths
one_line_summary: Visual and conceptual framework organizing the twelve pitch classes by perfect-fifth relationships, revealing key signatures, modulation paths, and harmonic distance.
band_notes: The visual diagram is an organizing schema; the underlying mathematical structure (cyclic group of order twelve under transposition) is rigorously formal.

name: Tonal Harmony
one_line_summary: Major-minor harmonic system governing Western art music roughly 1600-1900, organized around tonic-dominant relationships and functional progressions.

name: Functional Harmony
one_line_summary: Hugo Riemann's framework analyzing chord progressions through tonic, subdominant, and dominant functions and their substitutions.

name: Roman Numeral Analysis
one_line_summary: Analytical framework labeling chords by their scale-degree position relative to a key, foundational to common-practice harmonic analysis.

name: Figured Bass
one_line_summary: Baroque-era shorthand notation system using numerals beneath a bass line to indicate harmonic realization, foundational to Baroque ensemble practice.

name: Schenkerian Analysis
one_line_summary: Heinrich Schenker's hierarchical reduction analysis revealing background structures (Ursatz) underlying tonal masterworks.
band_notes: Schenker's writings include culturally chauvinist claims about German musical superiority that are rejected in contemporary scholarship even where the analytical method retains influence.

name: Pitch-Class Set Theory
one_line_summary: Allen Forte's framework analyzing atonal music through pitch-class sets characterized by interval-class content and equivalence under transposition and inversion.

name: Twelve-Tone Technique
one_line_summary: Schoenberg's compositional system organizing pitch material around ordered rows containing all twelve pitch classes, manipulated through transposition, inversion, and retrograde.

name: Integral Serialism
one_line_summary: Mid-20th-century extension of twelve-tone technique applying serial organization to rhythm, dynamics, and articulation, associated with Boulez and Stockhausen.

name: Neo-Riemannian Theory
one_line_summary: Late-20th-century transformational theory analyzing triadic relationships through parsimonious voice-leading operations (P, L, R), associated with Lewin, Hyer, and Cohn.

name: Just Intonation
one_line_summary: Tuning framework based on simple integer frequency ratios derived from the harmonic series, producing pure intervals at the cost of key flexibility.

name: Equal Temperament
one_line_summary: Tuning framework dividing the octave into twelve mathematically equal semitones, optimizing key flexibility at the cost of pure intervals.

name: Modal System
one_line_summary: Pre-tonal framework organizing pitch material through eight (later twelve) modes characterized by distinctive interval patterns and finals.

name: Sonata Form
one_line_summary: Compositional framework organizing movements into exposition, development, and recapitulation sections with characteristic key relationships, defining the Classical era.

name: Fugue
one_line_summary: Imitative contrapuntal procedure organized around a subject answered in related voices, formalized through Bach's practice and subsequent theoretical codification.

name: Species Counterpoint
one_line_summary: Johann Joseph Fux's pedagogical framework for teaching voice-leading through five graduated species, codified in Gradus ad Parnassum (1725).

name: Voice Leading Rules
one_line_summary: Body of rules governing the linear connection of voices in tonal harmony, of which species counterpoint is the pedagogical version.

name: Generative Theory of Tonal Music
one_line_summary: Lerdahl and Jackendoff's framework for tonal music cognition explicitly modeled on Chomskyan generative grammar, organized around grouping, metrical, time-span, and prolongational reductions.

name: Tonal Pitch Space
one_line_summary: Fred Lerdahl's spatial model of pitch relationships providing quantitative measures of harmonic distance grounded in cognitive empirical work.

name: Raga System
one_line_summary: Indian classical framework organizing melodic material through ragas characterized by ascending and descending scales, characteristic phrases, and affective and time-of-day associations.

name: Tala System
one_line_summary: Indian classical rhythmic framework organizing time through cyclic patterns (talas) with distinctive accent structures and characteristic divisions.

name: Maqam System
one_line_summary: Arabic, Turkish, and Persian framework organizing melodic material through modes (maqamat) with microtonal intervals and characteristic melodic phrases.

name: Pentatonic Theory
one_line_summary: Framework analyzing five-note scales central to East Asian, Celtic, blues, and many other musical traditions, with both major and minor pentatonic forms.

name: Nashville Number System
one_line_summary: Practical chord-progression notation system using scale-degree numbers, developed in Nashville studio practice and widely used in country and pop production.

name: Berklee Chord-Scale Theory
one_line_summary: Berklee College of Music's pedagogical framework matching scales to chord types for jazz improvisation, codifying earlier bebop practice.

name: Blues Form
one_line_summary: Compositional framework characterizing the twelve-bar blues progression with its characteristic harmonic motion and call-and-response phrase structure.
